item.title: [47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia] NATO Article 5 Is Not What You Think It Is
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
NATO Article 5 Is Not What You Think It Is

发布源: 47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia | 抓取时间: 2026-10-27

Login if you are already registered

President of the Russian International Affairs Council

Short versionof the article

Full versionof the article

There are few myths as captivating and durable as that of Article 5 of the 1949 Washington Treaty. Proponents of the myth are convinced that, thanks to this provision, NATO is like Alexandre Dumas’s Three Musketeers, in which an attack against one is an attack against all, and the US would automatically come in full force to the rescue of any of the allies under attack.

It’s debatable and essentially unknowable to what extent that would have worked in the situation of the Cold War, when the US genuinely feared the Soviet/Communist threat, because the bloc was never tested to that extent. But it certainly is utterly false under present conditions and likely future circumstances, and America’s allies and partners need to pay attention and be careful.

Ukraine lost its way and brought untold calamities upon itself when its leaders made NATO membership their goal. They didn’t realize that Washington never intended to give them even a symbolic guarantee of protection. Security in the 21st century world can’t be delegated to foreign powers, it can only rest on one’s own resources and stable relations with neighbors. This is the lesson not just for Ukraine and Europe, but also for the Gulf Arab states and East Asia.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在32. Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy, FKA Institute for the Economy in Transition --Russia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Monitoring legal regulation of the digital economy

发布源: 32. Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy, FKA Institute for the Economy in Transition --Russia | 抓取时间: 2026-10-27

Starting from 2024, Gaidar Institute launched a monthly review of international trends in the legal regulation of the digital economy. The purpose of Monitoring is to timely identify key developments and trends in the global practice of regulating the digital sector. The scientific and expert analysis allows not only to track current changes, but also to forecast their potential impact on the development of the digital industry in our country, contributing to the formation of an adaptive and effective strategy of legal regulation in this area.

It is published in Russian and English.
